issues.description: The problem statement (and the solution) expect a Stock.emptyStock() method (as listed in the UML and used in the solution), but the template Stock class defines a method named clearInventory() instead. This name mismatch is structural: students following the specification or the UML will look for emptyStock() and may attempt to call it (or implement SealSaloon relying on it), causing confusion or compilation errors because the template provides a differently named method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock API match the specification/solution by renaming clearInventory() to emptyStock(), or add a new emptyStock() method that delegates to clearInventory(). For example: public void emptyStock() { this.clearInventory(); } or rename the existing method to public void emptyStock() { this.stockIngredients = new StockIngredient[0]; }

issues.description: The Stock class method for clearing all ingredients is named clearInventory() in the template but is declared/provided as emptyStock() in the problem statement UML and implemented as emptyStock() in the solution. This mismatch can confuse students: the problem description expects an emptyStock() API and the solution uses emptyStock(), while the starter code exposes clearInventory(), causing a mapping barrier when students look for/implement the required method.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template API with the problem statement and solution by renaming the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock(), or add a small wrapper method emptyStock() that calls clearInventory(). Update any references or tests to use emptyStock().
